thread:
anna-cs: Hey devex, filing an escalation — customer reported a massive billing spike tied to a burst of 502/429s. They say our JS SDK retried and double-charged tokens. Any ideas?
eli-devex: ugh. Can you paste the customer request id + sample cURL?
anna-cs: request id cust-8821, sample attached in ticket: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <tok>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hello"}'` They saw 2 identical billed calls within ~200ms after a gateway 502.
sam-eng: quick Q — are they using our hosted API or dedicated?
anna-cs: hosted. Using JS SDK 3.2.0.
yu-ml: JS SDK 3.2.0 shipped a regen a few weeks ago, we had a header rename in OpenAPI that I thought was backwards-compatible. Might be related.
eli-devex: timeline: openapi PR merged 2106000000 -> regen happened in CI 2106500000 -> packages published. Any CI drift in clients?
regen-bot: regen job: openapi@main -> generated clients updated (ts,py,go) at 2106501234. Patch: changed parameter `client_request_id` -> `idempotency_key` and moved it from query -> header.
sam-eng: moving idempotency into header can change retry semantics if SDK doesn't forward the header consistently. Which SDK code path handles retries?
yu-ml: JS retry wrapper uses `idempotency_key` only if provided in options. If not, it auto-generates a key per attempt in 3.2.0 due to a bug — it regenerated on each retry instead of reusing. So retries became unique requests.
eli-devex: oh no — that would cause duplicate billing because server sees different idempotency keys per retry. Can we reproduce locally?
sam-eng: repro steps (quick):
```
# install exact sdk
npm i @redwood/sdk@3.2.0
# run a script that forces a 502 on first try
node repro.js
```
repro.js snippet:
```
const r = require('@redwood/sdk')
const client = new r.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW })
client.generate({ model: 'gpt-xl', input: 'test' }, { idempotencyKey: 'test-42' })
  .catch(e => console.log('err', e))
```
But in 3.2.0 the SDK ignores provided idempotencyKey in some internal codepath — it calls `genKey()` each try.
anna-cs: customer sent logs showing different x-idempotency headers: `x-rw-id: abc123` then `x-rw-id: abc456` for the retry. They billed for both.
eli-devex: are Python/Go SDKs affected?
yu-ml: python 2.1.4 pinned idempotency correctly. go client had a similar regen but used header correctly. Looks isolated to TS regen branch.
sam-eng: root cause summary: OpenAPI change moved param -> header, regen updated surface, but the TS SDK retry shim had a regression that regenerated idempotency on each attempt. CI didn't catch because we lack e2e test for idempotency header preservation under retry.
eli-devex: action items?
sam-eng: 1) hotfix TS SDK -> restore reuse of provided idempotencyKey and ensure generated key persists across retries. 2) publish patch 3.2.1 and notify customers. 3) add e2e CI test that simulates transient 502 and asserts header stable. 4) add a smoke test that checks published client package includes header code path.
anna-cs: customer asked for rollback to 3.1.x advice — should tell them to pin to 3.1.9 while we patch.
eli-devex: yep. Also add a billing credit checklist for affected customers.
yu-ml: created a minimal PR that fixes the reuse logic and adds unit tests: https://git.internal/redwood/regen-ts/pull/789
regen-bot: ci status: tests failed in integration step for node 16 on one matrix job (flaky network trigger) — investigating.
sam-eng: deploy-bot, can we cut a patch release even if one integration matrix is flaky? We need to coordinate with release owners.
deploy-bot: release policy allows patch releases with one failing non-blocking matrix if core tests pass. Please run `./scripts/release patch --cherry-pick 789`.
eli-devex: assign to @sam-eng and set ETA EOD. Anna, send customer a templated response: pin to 3.1.9 + we'll notify when 3.2.1 is out + we will audit billing.
anna-cs: done. Sent note and created billing ticket BT-442. Customer appreciated promptness :thumbsup:
sam-eng: handling changelog gap: regen job didn't include a clear changelog entry about idempotency header move. I'll add a post-regen checklist item to include a small changelog bullet and a playbook for header migrations.
yu-ml: also adding an automated lint rule: moving a parameter into headers should flag review and require e2e signoff.
eli-devex: good. After patch release, we should sweep support cases for duplicates and proactively credit where appropriate.
anna-cs: will queue the billing review. anyone wants to jump on the hotfix?
sam-eng: I'll own the PR and release. ETA 4 hours.
yu-ml: I'll follow up to add CI test later today.
eli-devex: thanks all. Closing internal thread when release is published.
anna-cs: thanks — I'll update customer and close loop. :white_check_mark:
